sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first. All three must load at startup before the app is ready. /healthz returns 503 until the load succeeds, then 200.
sonnet.q2: It retries (1 attempt plus 3 retries, 2s apart), logs the error class and secret name, exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and the old pods keep serving, so customers are not affected.
sonnet.q3: A background timer fires every 5 minutes (with jitter) and reads the latest version of each secret. If the version id changed and the value is non-empty and well-formed, it swaps the value in and logs the rotation. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning with the error class and retries on the next tick. It does not exit or fail readiness.
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory, in an in-memory map and an atomic reference, wrapped in SecretValue. They must never go to disk, environment variables or logs (including exception handlers and HTTP debug logs showing Authorization headers).
sonnet.q5: Read: only the orders-api-prod workload identity (plus decrypt on the prod KMS key). Write: only the security on-call engineer. Engineers have no read or write access to prod. Open question: engineers might read keys from pod memory if they can exec in.
sonnet.q6: The file is committed to git and git history is not rewritten, and old images embed the keys, so the old keys stay exposed and are treated as leaked. What makes them harmless is rotating them: new keys are issued, and the old keys are revoked (disabled, then deleted) at each provider.
sonnet.q7: Provider clients no longer copy the key in their constructor. Each request reads the current value through the secret accessor, which reads from an atomic reference. The refresh swaps in the new value, so a request sees either the old or the new one.
sonnet.q8: Check that every running pod, including leftover pods from the old set, logs the new version id for all three keys. Query the central log service (30-day retention). Run the check only after a full 5-minute refresh cycle since the last store write. Where available, provider per-key usage data must show no requests with old keys. Record the evidence in the migration log.
sonnet.q9: 1) Create store layout and access rules. 2) Issue new keys at providers, check them and write them to the store (old keys stay valid). 3) Move local dev off live keys (parallel with 2). 4) Merge the app code that reads from the store and remove api_key lines from the config, in one merge. 5) Roll out the image. 6) Confirm all pods use the new keys. 7) Revoke old keys one provider at a time. Then lock down rollback and clean up.
sonnet.q10: From the dev store under orders-api/dev/*, which holds sandbox or test keys (or a local stub if a provider has no sandbox). make run sets APP_ENV=dev and loads them through the developer's own identity. Prod keys never go on laptops.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED explicitly. The document says all three secrets must load before the app is ready, with retries, and after the last retry it logs the error class and secret name and exits non-zero, so the pod never becomes ready. A missing secret is not specifically addressed.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Rotation cadence is an open question for security. The plan does not choose a schedule, though it describes how a later rotation is done.
